contentBlocks.text: This week you built a claim, evidence, and a counterclaim/rebuttal. Today: put it all together!

A complete argumentative piece follows this structure: claim, evidence supporting it, the counterclaim, your rebuttal, and a closing statement restating your position. Assemble your complete argument using everything you've written this week, in that order, as one connected piece.
You just wrote a complete argumentative piece, start to finish! Tomorrow we'll review everything from this week.

objectives: Assemble a claim, evidence, counterclaim, rebuttal, and closing into one connected argumentative piece
Recognize the full 5-part structure of a complete argument
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Gather all of this week's pieces (claim, evidence, counterclaim, rebuttal).
2. Explain the full 5-part structure, including a new closing statement.
3. Have the child assemble their complete argument.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's cumulative review.
differentiationTips: Struggling: number each piece 1-5 in the order they'll appear before assembling, as a scaffold
Ready for more: ask the child to add one transition phrase connecting the evidence section to the counterclaim section
This is the payoff moment for the whole week — celebrate the finished argument as real, complete argumentative writing
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an assembly activity — check that all 5 pieces (claim, evidence, counterclaim, rebuttal, closing) appear in the correct order and connect logically as one argument.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Grade 6 Writing standard W.6.1a-e in full, synthesizing the whole week's argumentative-writing skills into one complete piece.

generationData.instructions: Assemble your complete argument: claim, evidence, counterclaim, rebuttal, and closing statement.
